subtitle: How a queen carved sacrifice into stone at a mountain gate

panels.shot: epic low-angle wide of a wind-swept mountain pass with carved cave façade
panels.action: Queen Naganika stands poised before the dark mouth of Naneghat cave, mist curling around the cliff as steep mountain paths and distant traders hint at the pass’s power.

dialogue.text: In the winds of Naneghat, Queen Naganika binds fire, soma and sacrifice into stone, and turns a mountain road into a throne for the Satavahanas.

i18n.hi: नाणेघाट की पवनों में रानी नागनिका अग्नि, सोम और यज्ञ को पत्थर में बाँधकर पहाड़ी राह को सातवाहनों का सिंहासन बना देती है।

panels.shot: bird’s-eye view sweeping along the Western Ghats ridge
panels.action: Rugged ridges of the Western Ghats rise like dark waves, a narrow cut of Naneghat climbing from the humid Konkan coast to the Deccan plateau under a pale sky.

dialogue.text: Between the sea of the Konkan and the stony Deccan runs a slit in the mountains: Naneghat, where caravans pant uphill and kingdoms breathe through a single pass.

i18n.hi: कोकण के सागर और पथरीले दक्कन के बीच पहाड़ों में एक दरार है—नाणेघाट, जहाँ बैलवाहन हांफते चढ़ते हैं और राज्य एक ही दर्रे से साँस लेते हैं।

panels.shot: mid-wide along the path showing traders and soldiers crossing each other
panels.action: A long line of traders with pack-bulls and baskets of goods winds uphill as a small armed escort descends, both streams squeezing past each other on the rocky ledge.

dialogue.text: Salt from the coast, cotton from the plateau, coins and gossip from far cities — all grind past these rocks. Whoever claims this road touches the veins of the western Deccan.

i18n.hi: तट का नमक, पठार की रूई, दूर नगरों के सिक्के और खबरें—सब इन चट्टानों के बीच रगड़ खाते गुजरते हैं। जो इस राह का मालिक है, वह पश्चिमी दक्कन की नसें पकड़ लेता है।

panels.shot: slow push-in from behind Naganika looking down the pass toward the distant sea
panels.action: Queen Naganika stands cloaked at a ledge, hair bound, jewelry restrained, gazing down the long cut of Naneghat toward the hazy shimmer of the distant Konkan.

dialogue.text: Around the first century before the Common Era, a Satavahana queen looks down this gorge and sees more than stone. She sees a stage on which power can be performed.

i18n.hi: ईसा से पहले पहली सदी के आस‑पास एक सातवाहन रानी इस घाट को देखती है। उसे केवल पत्थर नहीं दिखता, उसे सत्ता का मंच दिखता है।

panels.shot: medium close-up profile of Naganika with faint superimposed silhouettes of kings behind her
panels.action: In profile, Naganika’s calm face is lit by soft light; behind her, faint ghostly silhouettes suggest a line of Satavahana rulers and elders who came before.

dialogue.text: Her name is Naganika, daughter of a proud line, wife of Satakarni. Around her, older powers jostle: Shungas in the north, local chiefs in the west, restless clans on the plateau.

i18n.hi: उसका नाम नागनिका है—गौरवशाली वंश की बेटी, सातकर्णि की रानी। उसके चारों ओर पुरानी ताकतें भिड़ती हैं: उत्तर में शुंग, पश्चिम के मुखिया, पठार के बेचैन कुळ।

panels.shot: intimate interior shot of a simple hall, focus on inscriptions and ritual objects laid before her
panels.action: In a modest wooden hall, Naganika sits on a low seat with palm-leaf drafts, ritual ladles and a small model of a horse before her, counselors’ hands reaching into frame.

dialogue.text: We do not hear her private counsel, but the stone she leaves tells us this: she chooses the oldest, most demanding Vedic rites to proclaim Satavahana kingship.

i18n.hi: उसकी निजी सलाह हम नहीं सुनते, पर उसका छोड़ा पत्थर यह कहता है: वह सातवाहन राजसत्ता जताने को सबसे प्राचीन, कठिन वैदिक यज्ञ चुनती है।

panels.shot: dramatic low-angle wide of an ashvamedha ground with ritual posts and a tethered horse
panels.action: On an open field, an unblemished horse stands tethered near carved posts, brahman priests seated in rows as smoke rises from newly built brick altars.

dialogue.text: Ashvamedha. Rajasuya. Vajapeya. In her inscription, Naganika carefully lists these srauta sacrifices, as if each rite were a pillar raising her husband’s throne.

i18n.hi: अश्वमेध। राजसूय। वाजपेय। अपने लेख में नागनिका ये श्रोत्रिय यज्ञ गिनती है, मानो हर अनुष्ठान उसके पति के सिंहासन का एक खंभा हो।

panels.shot: close shot of priests around a fire altar, ladle poised above the flames
panels.action: Brahman priests sit cross-legged around a square fire altar, one priest’s hand frozen mid-pour as clarified butter hangs in the ladle over the glowing embers.

dialogue.text: Fire blazes, mantras roll, priests pour ghee and soma. These rites do more than feed gods; they announce that Satakarni is a king among kings, bound to old Vedic law.

i18n.hi: अग्नि भड़कती है, मंत्र गूंजते हैं, पुरोहित घी और सोम उँडेलते हैं। ये यज्ञ केवल देवता नहीं, यह भी घोषित करते हैं कि सातकर्णि राजाओं में राजा है, पुराने वेद–धर्म से बंधा।

panels.shot: wide shot of a sacrificial field filled with lines of cattle, horses, elephants and attendants
panels.action: Rows of cattle, a few sturdy horses and a couple of elephants stand with handlers on the ritual ground, their forms receding into the distance under the watch of officials.

dialogue.text: The Naneghat text lists gifts with care: cattle, horses, elephants, gold. Some numbers have faded, but the scale remains clear. Sacrifice here is also spectacle and distribution.

i18n.hi: नाणेघाट के लेख में दान भी सावधानी से दर्ज हैं: गौ, घोड़े, हाथी, सोना। कुछ अंक मिट गए हैं, पर पैमाना साफ है—यहाँ यज्ञ भी तमाशा है, भीड़ में बाँटने का भोज है।

panels.shot: tight shot of hands weighing coins and a tray of ornaments beside a priest
panels.action: A pair of strong hands pours coins onto a tray beside neatly arranged ornaments, while a priest’s hand points to a list scratched on a palm leaf.

dialogue.text: Gold and goods flow to brahmans. In return flow verses, lineages, blessings. This is political theology in practice: wealth turned into words that fix a family’s place in the world.

i18n.hi: सोना और वस्तु ब्राह्मणों तक बहती है। बदले में श्लोक, वंश, आशीर्वाद लौटते हैं। यही राजधर्म की थियरी है—धन को शब्दों में बदलना, जो कुळ की जगह जग में ठोक दे।

panels.shot: cutaway interior shot of a simple rock-cut hall with early Buddhist monks receiving alms from attendants
panels.action: In a bare rock-cut hall elsewhere, monks in simple robes sit quietly as attendants place bowls of grain and cloth before them, a contrast to the ritual bustle of the sacrifice ground.

dialogue.text: Yet the same Satavahana house also gives to monks in other caves. Patronage flows along more than one track. Naganika’s world is not a neat contest of single faiths.

i18n.hi: इसी सातवाहन घराने से दूसरे गुफाओं के भिक्षुओं को भी दान जाता है। कृपा कई पटरियों पर बहती है। नागनिका की दुनिया कोई एक धर्म की साफ रेखा नहीं।

panels.shot: medium shot of Naganika overseeing scribes beside a rough cave wall mock-up
panels.action: Naganika stands while scribes sit on the floor before a rough slab, practicing letters in Prakrit as she watches, a hand resting on a rolled manuscript.

dialogue.text: Now she takes the next step. Rituals vanish with smoke; gifts disappear with time. She will bind them in script. She chooses Maharashtri Prakrit, the speech of her land, not distant Sanskrit.

i18n.hi: अब वह अगला कदम उठाती है। यज्ञ धुएँ में उड़ जाते हैं, दान समय के साथ खो जाते हैं। वह इन्हें लेख में बाँध देगी। वह अपने देश की बोली माहाराष्ट्रि प्राकृत चुनती है, दूर की संस्कृत नहीं।

panels.shot: low-angle shot in front of the Naneghat cave façade with masons working the inscription space
panels.action: Masons chip at the flat rock wall of the emerging cave, a cleared rectangular panel waiting for text as Naganika stands nearby, framed by scaffolding against the cliff.

dialogue.text: At Naneghat, workers carve a cave into the cliff. On its wall, a broad panel is smoothed. Here Naganika will place her inscription, facing merchants and messengers who pass.

i18n.hi: नाणेघाट पर मजदूर चट्टान काटकर गुफा बनाते हैं। दीवार पर चौड़ा हिस्सा समतल किया जाता है। यहीं नागनिका अपना लेख जमाएगी, सामने से गुजरते बनियों और दूतों की ओर।

panels.shot: extreme close-up on chisel tip carving early Brahmi letters into rock
panels.action: The sharp tip of a chisel bites into stone, a cloud of rock dust catching the light as the curves of an early Brahmi letter slowly emerge.

dialogue.text: Letter by letter, the rock drinks her words. In this script, Satakarni’s titles, her own name, her parents and sons, and the list of sacrifices take permanent form.

i18n.hi: अक्षर‑अक्षर कर पत्थर उसके शब्द पीता है। इसी लिपि में सातकर्णि के उपाधि, उसका अपना नाम, उसके माता‑पिता, पुत्र और यज्ञों की सूची अमर आकार लेती है।

panels.shot: medium close-up of Naganika reading freshly carved lines by torchlight
panels.action: By flickering torchlight, Naganika leans close to the fresh inscription, her fingers hovering just above the grooves, eyes intent as shadows dance across the letters.

dialogue.speaker: queen_naganika
dialogue.text: Let every who climbs this ghat know whose fire burned, whose gifts flowed.

i18n.hi: जो भी इस घाट पर चढ़े, जान ले किसकी अग्नि जली, किसके दान बहे।

panels.shot: wide shot inside the cave showing donors’ portraits niches and traders resting nearby
panels.action: Within the cave, rough niches suggesting royal figures overlook resting traders and porters who sit on the stone ledge, some glancing at the inscription as they share food.

dialogue.text: This is no hidden shrine. Naneghat is a public road. Men hauling salt and cloth, officers leading escorts, wandering storytellers — all can rest here under her carved genealogy.

i18n.hi: यह कोई छुपी देवालय नहीं। नाणेघाट सार्वजनिक राह है। नमक और कपड़ा ढोने वाले, फौजी दस्तों के अफसर, भटकते कथावाचक—सब यहाँ उसकी खुदी वंशावली के नीचे दम ले सकते हैं।

panels.shot: medium shot of a traveling brahman tracing the letters with his hand while others listen
panels.action: A traveling brahman stands by the inscription, finger following the lines as a small circle of listeners watches, their faces lit by early morning light streaming into the cave.

dialogue.text: Some hear the words aloud from learned mouths. Others simply see the royal names and offerings. Either way, the message seeps in: this pass lies in the orbit of Satavahana ritual power.

i18n.hi: कुछ लोग विद्वानों से यह लेख सुनते हैं, कुछ केवल राजनाम और दान देखते हैं। किसी भी तरह संदेश रिसता है: यह दर्रा सातवाहन यज्ञ–शक्ति की परिधि में है।

panels.shot: time-lapse style wide showing the same cave wall eroding over centuries, letters fading
panels.action: The same inscription wall is shown with softened edges, faint letters and patches of erosion, suggesting centuries of wind and rain working on the stone.

dialogue.text: Centuries pass. Rain eats at the rock. Some numbers blur, some lines break. The ashvamedha, rajasuya and gifts are still there, but partly veiled by time’s hand.

i18n.hi: सदियाँ बीतती हैं। वर्षा पत्थर कुतरती है। कुछ अंक धुंधले, कुछ पंक्तियाँ टूटीं। अश्वमेध, राजसूय और दान अब भी हैं, पर समय की परत से आधे ढँके।

panels.shot: modern-era archaeologist’s low-angle silhouette studying the wall with notebook in hand
panels.action: A modern scholar’s silhouette stands before the same wall, notebook and camera in hand, studying the script carefully as soft daylight washes the faded inscription.

dialogue.text: In our age, epigraphists lean close with notebooks and cameras, tracing the old Brahmi strokes, arguing over missing numerals, rebuilding Naganika’s world from these damaged lines.

i18n.hi: आज हमारे युग में शिलालेख‑विद्वान नोटबुक और कैमरा लेकर झुकते हैं, पुराने ब्राह्मी अक्षर टटोलते, खोए अंकों पर बहस करते, इन्हीं घिसी पंक्तियों से नागनिका की दुनिया जोड़ते हैं।

panels.shot: poetic split-scene: half shows Naganika at the cave, half the faded inscription today
panels.action: The frame splits: on one side, Naganika stands in fresh Naneghat, on the other, the same wall worn and cracked, the queen now only a memory behind the script.

dialogue.text: Legend remembered kings; the stone preserved the queen. Through Naneghat, we see Naganika not as a shadow behind Satakarni, but as the hand that turned sacrifice into policy.

i18n.hi: किंवदंतियों ने राजाओं को याद रखा, पत्थर ने रानी को। नाणेघाट के जरिये हम नागनिका को सातकर्णि की छाया नहीं, उस हाथ के रूप में देखते हैं जिसने यज्ञ को नीति में बदला।

panels.shot: final wide pull-back from the Naneghat pass showing road, cave and distant plateau
panels.action: The view pulls back from the cave mouth to reveal the winding road of Naneghat clinging to the mountain, the Konkan haze behind and the Deccan plateau stretching ahead.

dialogue.text: At this mountain gate, Naganika showed that rule is not only won in battlefields, but inscribed in ritual, gifts and stone — a lesson in how power is performed long before it is obeyed.

i18n.hi: इस पहाड़ी द्वार पर नागनिका दिखाती है कि राज केवल रणभूमि में नहीं जीता जाता, बल्कि यज्ञ, दान और पत्थर में लिखा जाता है—सत्ता कैसे निभाई जाती है, यह पाठ आज्ञा से बहुत पहले।

subtitle_i18n.en: How a queen carved sacrifice into stone at a mountain gate
subtitle_i18n.hi: कैसे एक रानी ने पहाड़ी द्वार पर बलि को पत्थर में उकेरा
